The defendant did not make payment of the outstanding amount.
The plaintiff accordingly sent legal notice on 16.09.2024, the tracking report whereof suggests that the same was duly served upon the defendant.
No reply thereto was furnished by the defendant.

3. Therefore, the plaintiff has filed the instant suit against the defendant, inter alia seeking a decree in the sum of Rs.3,65,582/- (Rupees Three Lakhs Sixty Five Thousand Five Hundred Eighty Two Only) alongwith interest @ 18% per annum w.e.f 06.07.2022 till realization thereof.
4. It is pertinent to mention here that prior to filing the present suit, plaintiff had also exhausted the remedy of pre-institution mediation in terms of Section 12-A of Commercial Courts Act, 2015.
The defendant refused to participate in the pre-institution mediation.
Accordingly, Certificate of Non-Starter Report dated 22.11.2024 was issued in the matter.

5. After getting served with the summons, defendant filed written statement, inter alia denying the receipt of goods in one breath and CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 questioning the quality of goods in another breath.

The reference was made to FIR No.585/2022, U/s 420/272/273/120-B IPC, PS Mangolpuri, lodged by one Shri Jitender Singh against the plaintiff, wherein there were allegations of supply of spurious and sub-standard quality of kiryana goods by the plaintiff to his that customer.
The defendant has questioned the entitlement of plaintiff to recover the suit amount from it on the basis of aforesaid FIR.
6. Plaintiff filed replication, inter alia denying the averments made in the written statement and reiterating the ones made in the plaint.

OPP.

My issue wise findings in the matter are as under.

13. Issue No.(i):
Whether the plaintiff is entitled to decree of the suit amount, as prayed for?

OPP. 
The onus to prove this issue was upon the plaintiff.

The learned counsel for the plaintiff has very vehemently argued that the goods were supplied to the defendant through Invoices Ex.PW1/4 (Colly) on various dates; the ledger account in respect thereof has been duly proved on record as Ex.PW1/3.

It is next contended that the defendant never questioned either the receipt of goods or quality thereof at any stage,
except for a complaint dated 30.05.2022 Ex.DW1/6, wherein defendant categorically admitted receipt of the goods, however, questioned the quality of goods on the premise that an FIR had been registered by the police against the plaintiff for supplying spurious material to some other person.
It was nowhere mentioned in the said complaint that the material supplied by the plaintiff to the defendant was not received.

Even there has CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 not been mention of any customer of the defendant having pointed out the defect in the goods sold by it to them.

14. It is next contended that the legal notice Ex.PW1/5 was correctly addressed to the defendant and despite presumption of the service thereof, the defendant did not file any reply thereto and as such,
the defendant did not have any defence to deny outstanding payment to the plaintiff.
15.

Per contra, learned counsel for the defendant has very vehemently argued that PW-1/Shri Anshul Bansal has no authority to depose on behalf of plaintiff as the SPA Ex.PW1/2 does not bear acknowledgment or acceptance by him.
It is next contended that the defendant did not receive the material mentioned in invoices as the invoices neither bear the signatures nor stamp of plaintiff nor that of defendant.

It is next contended that the ledger account filed by the plaintiff cannot be believed to be correct, as it is not accompanied by any duly audited balance-sheet showing the name of defendant in the list of creditors.

The learned counsel has termed the invoices Ex.PW1/4 (Colly)
as forged and fabricated.

16. As regards the argument of learned counsel for the defendant that Ex.PW1/2 is not a valid attorney authorizing PW-1 to depose on behalf of plaintiff in the matter for want of signatures of this witness on this document, it is noted that the law does not require the Authorized CS (Comm)
No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD: 04.09.2025 Representative to have his acknowledgment on the attorney.
The requirement of law simply is that an attorney can depose on behalf of plaintiff regarding facts to the extent of his knowledge of the facts which happened in his knowledge.

In one breath the defendant has questioned the authority of PW-1 to depose in the matter, but in the same breath the attorney issued by defendant in the name of DW-1 also does not bear his signature towards acknowledgment, making him an Authorized Representative of defendant.

In any case, the defendant has not disputed the trade relations between the parties and it having purchased the material from the plaintiff.

The invoices have been termed to be forged and fabricated, but no complaint worth the name has been placed on record by the defendant to show that after coming to know of the forgery of invoices, recourse to the legal remedies available to it was taken.
No complaint of forgery or even an application under Section 340 Cr.P.C has been filed before the Court.

18. As regards the argument of learned counsel for the defendant that the goods supplied were spurious, there is no material worth the name about the quality or otherwise of goods, firstly there is no notice under Section 42 of the Sales of Goods Act, 1930 (hereinafter referred to as the "Act"),

sentences.text: The trial court has rejected the defence of the appellant/defendant, praying for dismissal of the suit, while holding that the appellant/defendant has failed to prove that the said defective goods were returned as the Challan documents/Ex.DW1/1 and Ex.DW1/2 did not bear any signatures on the receipt of the respondent/plaintiff of the alleged defective materials which were claimed to have been returned by the appellant/defendant, owing to the fact that Section 42 of the Sale of Goods Act, 1930 provides that goods are deemed to be accepted if rejection of the goods is not communicated in reasonable period of time.

It is noted that for the first Bill no.01 dated 15.05.2000, the reasonable period would be one month i.e. up to 15.06.2000,
and for the Bill no.07 dated 10.07.2000 the period of one month would expire on 10.08.2000 and for the third Bill no.011 dated 30.9.2000 the period would expire on 30.10.2000.

Admittedly, in these periods of 30 days after receipt of the goods, no intimation has been proved by the appellant/defendant which they have served upon the respondent/plaintiff in terms of Section 42 of Sale of Goods Act about the goods supplied by the respondent/plaintiff to the appellant/defendant of being defective.

Even the so- called Challans Ex.DW1/1 and Ex.DW1/2 which in any case have not been proved to show the return of goods by the appellant/defendant to the respondent/plaintiff with the fact that these Challans are dated 30.03.2001, and the date of 30.03.2001 is not a reasonable period as per Section 42 of the Sale CS (Comm) No.774/2024: M/s Balaji Trading Company V/s M/s SKB Traders: DOD:

(i) The defendant did not prefer to send any reply to the legal notice of plaintiff (Ex.PW1/5),
inter alia complaining about the quality of goods received by it from the plaintiff.

The Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case reported as, "1980 RLR (Note 44)", titled as, "Kalu Ram V/s Sita Ram" has been pleased to hold that adverse presumption will be drawn if the legal notice is not replied to.

The relevant portion of the said judgment reads as under:
xxxxx "It was held that the plaintiff before filing suit had served defendant with a notice making serious allegations that defendant was a trespasser and that his possession was illegal.
Defendant did not refute these charges and remained silent by ignoring to reply the notice.
Silence showed that he had nothing to deny and hence it was a fit case for raising adverse presumption.
Besides the defendant also failed to prove the two contentions that he had raised.
There is nothing on record to support the pleas that he had taken.
His appeal is without force.
The appeal of the plaintiff is supported by the provisions of O. 20 R.12, CPC and trial court should have ordered mesne profits till the delivery of possession.
Plaintiff is held entitled to same."

xxxxx (Emphasis supplied)

There is another aspect of the matter which negates the argument of the respondent and that is that the appellant served a legal notice on the respondent vide Ex. PW-1/3.
No reply the same was given by the respondent.
But inspite of the same no adverse inference was drawn against the respondent.

This Court in the case of Kalu Ram v. Sita Ram 1980 RLR (Note) 44 observed that service of notice having been admitted without reservation and that having not been replied in that eventuality adverse inference should be drawn because he kept quite over the notice and did not send any reply.

As regards the quantum of interest, it is noted that the invoices (Ex.PW1/4 Colly)
does not stipulate any contractual rate of interest in case of delayed payments,
however, the learned counsel for the plaintiff has prayed for grant of interest @18%
per annum on the delayed payments.

Though, the transaction between the parties is commercial in nature, however, I am of the considered opinion that grant of interest @18% per annum is on higher side and instead grant of interest @12% per annum on the delayed payments would meet the ends of justice.
I order accordingly.
Relief 27.

In view of the above, suit of the plaintiff is decreed as under:

(ii) Plaintiff is also held entitled to counsel's fee which is quantified as Rs.22,000/- as also costs.
28. Decree Sheet be drawn accordingly.
